children.name: (1) Diagnosis of moderately to severely active rhe
children.source_text: (1) Diagnosis of moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis
children.search_description: The patient must have a confirmed diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) that is documented as moderately to severely active. Look for explicit statements of the diagnosis in the assessment or problem list, often accompanied by severity indicators, disease activity scores (e.g., DAS28, CDAI, SDAI), or descriptions of symptoms like persistent joint swelling, tenderness, and functional impairment consistent with moderate to severe disease. Evidence of erosive disease or extra-articular manifestations may also support severity.

children.name: (a) History of failure to a 3 month trial of one n
children.source_text: (a) History of failure to a 3 month trial of one non-biologic disease modifying anti-rheumatic drug (DMARD) [e.g., methotrexate, leflunomide, sulfasalazine, hydroxychloroquine] at the maximally indicated doses, unless contraindicated or clinically significant adverse effects are experienced (document drug, date, and duration of trial)b
children.search_description: The patient must have previously taken at least one of the specified non-biologic DMARDs (methotrexate, leflunomide, sulfasalazine, or hydroxychloroquine) for a minimum of 3 months at maximally indicated doses, and this trial must have 'failed'. Failure is indicated by documentation of inadequate response, lack of efficacy, progression of disease, or discontinuation due to clinically significant adverse effects or intolerance. This evidence typically appears in the medication history, past medical history, or assessment and plan sections. Discontinuation due to disease remission or successful treatment does NOT count as failure.

children.name: (b) Patient has been previously treated with a sys
children.source_text: (b) Patient has been previously treated with a systemic targeted immunomodulator FDA-approved for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis as documented by claims history or submission of medical records (Document drug, date, and duration of therapy) [e.g., Enbrel (etanercept), Cimzia (certolizumab), Simponi (golimumab), Orencia (abatacept), Xeljanz (tofacitinib), Olumiant (baricitinib), Rinvoq (upadacitinib)]
children.search_description: The patient must have a documented history of having been treated previously with at least one of the listed systemic targeted immunomodulators (Enbrel/etanercept, Cimzia/certolizumab, Simponi/golimumab, Orencia/abatacept, Xeljanz/tofacitinib, Olumiant/baricitinib, Rinvoq/upadacitinib) for rheumatoid arthritis. This evidence can be found in past medication lists, treatment history, or notes describing prior therapies. The criterion requires *prior treatment*, not necessarily current use or a documented failure.

children.name: i. Patient is currently on adalimumab therapy as d
children.source_text: i. Patient is currently on adalimumab therapy as documented by claims history or submission of medical records (Document date and duration of therapy):
children.search_description: The patient must be actively receiving adalimumab therapy. Look for adalimumab (Humira) in the current medication list, active prescriptions, recent refill records, or in the assessment and plan section with phrases indicating ongoing use. This excludes past use, planned initiation, or discontinuation.

children.name: i. Patient is currently on adalimumab therapy

evidence_requirements.source_text: as documented by claims history or submission of medical records (Document date and duration of therapy)

children.name: ii. Patient has not received a manufacturer suppli
children.source_text: ii. Patient has not received a manufacturer supplied sample at no cost in the prescriber's office, or any form of assistance from a manufacturer sponsored program (e.g., sample card which can be redeemed at a pharmacy for a free supply of medication) as a means to establish as a current user of adalimumab*
children.search_description: This is a negated criterion, meaning the patient must NOT have received adalimumab through free samples or manufacturer assistance programs. The criterion is met if there is NO mention in the clinical notes or claims history of the patient receiving free manufacturer samples, sample cards, or any form of manufacturer-sponsored patient assistance or bridge program for adalimumab. If such mentions exist, the criterion is NOT met.

children.name: (3) Patient is not receiving adalimumab in combina
children.source_text: (3) Patient is not receiving adalimumab in combination with another systemic targeted immunomodulator. [e.g., Enbrel (etanercept), Cimzia (certolizumab), Simponi (golimumab), Orencia (abatacept), Xeljanz (tofacitinib), Olumiant (baricitinib), Rinvoq (upadacitinib)] for treatment of the same indication.
children.search_description: This is a negated criterion, meaning the patient must NOT be receiving adalimumab in combination with any other systemic targeted immunomodulator listed (e.g., etanercept, certolizumab, golimumab, abatacept, tofacitinib, baricitinib, upadacitinib) for the same indication (rheumatoid arthritis). The criterion is met if there is NO mention of concurrent use of adalimumab with any of these other drugs. If there is documentation of such combination therapy, the criterion is NOT met.

children.name: (4) Prescribed by or in consultation with a rheuma
children.source_text: (4) Prescribed by or in consultation with a rheumatologist
children.search_description: The prescription for the requested therapy (presumably adalimumab) must originate from a rheumatologist, or documentation must clearly indicate that a rheumatologist has been consulted regarding the patient's rheumatoid arthritis management and has approved or recommended the specific treatment. Look for 'rheumatologist' in the provider's signature block, consultation notes, referral information, or in the patient's treatment plan discussion.
